requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.fingerprints` has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence, and it has no implementation roots.

I checked each clause:

- **"Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`".** This names an algorithm, but it only restates the digest that `requirements.references.structural_hash` defines: "the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding". Any hashing library or call structure that yields the same SHA-256 digest of the same encoding satisfies it. Switching crates or wrapping the hash in a different helper changes nothing observable, so the library is discretionary. Only a different digest algorithm would break the clause, and that would show up in the hash value, so it is behavior. The encoding rules live in the cited requirement, and they are also behavioral: word splitting, `ab cd` versus `abcd`, comment exclusion and the doc-comment groups. The text cites that requirement and does not refine it.
- **"The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`".** The scheme is a string the loaded contents report, and the cited requirement owns the `OutlineLang::fingerprint_scheme` and `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme` signatures. This text prescribes no signature or type of its own. Any storage or derivation of that string that identifies the rules and version behaves the same.
- **"Comments are excluded from structural hashes."** This is an observable property: editing a comment does not change the hash. A different internal way of skipping comments, such as filtering tokens or stripping text beforehand, gives the same results. It is not structural.

The mandatory inputs are the requirement itself, `requirements.references.structural_hash` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`. The first has no `Implements` edges, and I also found none on `requirements.references.structural_hash`. The structural parts of the cited requirements belong to those requirements' own assessments. Nothing here needs an implementation reference.

behavioral: Obligations and the tests that cover them for `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.fingerprints`:

1. **Comments are excluded from YAML structural hashes.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has an `a.yml` case on selector `pair[a]`. A standalone comment and a trailing comment can be changed or removed, and the hash stays equal. Changing the non-comment value `1` to `2` changes the hash, so the test is not trivially passing. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` repeats the comment-exclusion check for YAML with `# note` against `# edited`.

2. **Whitespace-separated words, with word boundaries preserved.** In the same `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` test, the YAML case changes `"two words"` to `"two   words"`, and the hash is unchanged. Joining the words as `"twowords"` changes the hash. This checks that whitespace is not hashed and that each word is encoded separately.

3. **SHA-256 digest.** The same test asserts that the saved hash is 64 hex digits. The SHA-256 rules themselves are specified and tested under the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which I did not reassess. The tests here check the digest's form, and the digest changes only when the structure or words change.

4. **Fingerprint scheme.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` has a YAML case. Its `check` helper asserts `language.fingerprint_scheme()` equals `"yaml-structural-v1"`. It does this for both the `Yaml` value and its default. It also asserts that contents loaded from source retain that scheme. Scheme retention in general is covered by the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, which I did not reassess.

All three tests carry `{test}` markers for `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.fingerprints`. I found no obligation in the subject that lacks test evidence.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
